note: Day 1 is startDate. Change startDate to reset the plan. Regulatory items are written as calls to make and things to confirm, not as legal advice — verify every requirement with the agency named.

days.focus: Make sure the business legally exists

tasks.title: Confirm your LLC is active on Sunbiz
tasks.detail: search.sunbiz.org, look up Peak Bio-Clean. Check the status says ACTIVE and the annual report isn't overdue. If nothing comes up, file the LLC today.

tasks.title: Confirm you have an EIN
tasks.detail: Free from irs.gov, takes 10 minutes online. You cannot open a business bank account or get insurance without it.

tasks.title: Open a business checking account
tasks.detail: Bring the EIN letter and Sunbiz filing. Keeping business and personal money separate is what makes the LLC actually protect you.

days.focus: Insurance quotes, the thing that gates every commercial account

tasks.title: Get three general liability quotes
tasks.detail: Tell every agent specifically: biohazard remediation, trauma and crime scene cleanup. Some carriers won't write it. You want an agent who has placed this class before.

tasks.title: Ask each one about pollution / environmental liability
tasks.detail: General liability usually excludes contamination. In this trade that exclusion is the whole job. Ask for it as an endorsement or separate policy.

tasks.title: Ask what a certificate of insurance costs to issue
tasks.detail: Property managers and funeral homes will ask for a COI naming them. You need to know you can produce one same-day.

days.focus: Biomedical waste, the part most new operators get wrong

tasks.title: Call your county health department
tasks.detail: Ask directly: what registration do I need to transport biomedical waste in this county, and do I need a generator permit if I store it. Florida regulates this under Chapter 64E-16, administered county by county. Write down who you spoke to.

tasks.title: Ask what the application costs and how long it takes
tasks.detail: You need this on the calendar before you take a job that generates regulated waste.

tasks.title: Save the answers into Second Brain
tasks.detail: Title it Biomedical Waste Registration. Six months from now you will not remember what they told you.

days.focus: Line up where the waste actually goes

tasks.title: Get pricing from two medical waste disposal vendors
tasks.detail: Stericycle and a regional competitor. Ask for per-box and per-pickup pricing, minimum contract term, and whether they do on-call pickups for small operators.

tasks.title: Ask whether they'll take trauma waste from a non-medical generator
tasks.detail: Not all of them will. Find this out now, not on a job.

tasks.title: Log both quotes in Second Brain under Vendor / Partner

days.focus: Decide what you sell and what it costs

tasks.title: Write your service list with a price range for each
tasks.detail: Unattended death, suicide, homicide, hoarding, gross filth, vehicle, rodent, odor. Range not fixed price. You'll quote on scope, but you need a starting number when someone calls.

tasks.title: Write your minimum job price
tasks.detail: The number below which a job costs you money once you count PPE, disposal, drive time and your day.

tasks.title: Save it as Pricing in Second Brain
Create or claim your Google Business Profile
tasks.detail: Free. This is the single highest-value marketing asset for a local service business, above your website and far above Instagram.

tasks.title: Start verification
tasks.detail: It's usually a postcard and takes a week or two, so starting today matters.

tasks.title: Add every service category and your full service area
Check what's still open from days 1 through 6
tasks.detail: Insurance quotes and health department callbacks usually lag. Chase them today.

tasks.title: Open the dashboard and confirm the week's activity logged correctly
Write your Exposure Control Plan
tasks.detail: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires a written plan for anyone with occupational exposure to blood. OSHA publishes a model plan on osha.gov, start from that and make it yours.

tasks.title: Decide your hepatitis B vaccination policy
tasks.detail: If you hire anyone, you must offer the vaccine series at no cost within 10 days of assignment. Know what that costs before you hire.

tasks.title: Save the finished plan into Second Brain under Compliance
Read OSHA 1910.134 and write down what applies to you
tasks.detail: If you require a respirator, you generally need a written program, a medical evaluation, and a fit test before first use. This is the standard that gets small operators cited.

tasks.title: Price a medical evaluation and fit test locally
tasks.detail: Occupational health clinics do both, often in one visit.

tasks.title: Book yours
Build an SDS binder
tasks.detail: Safety Data Sheet for every chemical you carry. Download from each manufacturer. Keep a copy in the truck.

tasks.title: Confirm your disinfectants are EPA-registered for the pathogens you claim to kill
tasks.detail: Check the EPA registration number and the label's kill claims. Your marketing cannot claim more than the label does.

tasks.title: Price two certification paths
tasks.detail: IICRC and ABRA are the two names commercial accounts recognize. Get real numbers on cost and time.

tasks.title: Pick one and put the date on the calendar
tasks.detail: You do not need it to start working, but it shortens every partner conversation and you'll want it before pitching insurance adjusters.

tasks.title: Inventory your PPE and consumables
tasks.detail: Suits, respirators and cartridges, gloves, boot covers, sharps containers, red bags, disinfectant, HEPA filtration, hand tools.

tasks.title: Write your restock threshold
tasks.detail: The point at which you reorder rather than discovering you're short at 2am.

tasks.title: Price a full job's worth of consumables
tasks.detail: This number goes into your minimum job price.

days.focus: Paperwork you'll use on every job

tasks.title: Build a work authorization form
tasks.detail: Signed before you touch anything. Names who is authorizing, the scope, and who is paying.

tasks.title: Build a scope sheet and a waste log
tasks.detail: What you removed, what was disposed, where it went, who signed for it.

tasks.title: Save all three into Second Brain under Contract
Confirm insurance is bound or close to it
Confirm the waste registration is filed or scheduled
Everything in weeks one and two is what lets a property manager say yes. Chase whatever is still open.
Build a list of 20 funeral homes within an hour's drive
tasks.detail: Google Maps, get the name, phone, and the director if the site lists one.

tasks.title: Add all 20 to the dashboard as leads
tasks.detail: Set the ICP to Funeral Homes & Decedent Transport.

tasks.title: Give every one of them a follow-up date
tasks.detail: This is what fills your Morning Briefing tomorrow.

tasks.title: Call or email all 20
tasks.detail: Use the vendor packet email in the dashboard. It's already written.

tasks.title: Log every single attempt
tasks.detail: Including no-answers. Unlogged work is invisible work.

tasks.title: Set the next follow-up before closing each lead
Build a list of 20 property management companies and HOA managers
tasks.detail: These are your highest-repeat customers. Unattended deaths in rentals, evictions, gross filth turnovers.

tasks.title: Add them to the dashboard with follow-up dates
Send the first ten
Build a list of 20 restoration and plumbing companies
tasks.detail: They hit biohazard jobs they don't want and need someone to hand them to. This is the fastest referral source to activate.

tasks.title: Add them and send the first ten
tasks.detail: The pitch is different here: you're the subcontractor who takes the job they can't do.

tasks.title: Open Morning Briefing and clear every overdue follow-up
tasks.detail: By now you have 60 leads in the system. This is the day the dashboard starts earning its keep.

tasks.title: Second touch on anyone who didn't answer the first
Update the vendor packet with what you've built
tasks.detail: Insurance, waste registration, certification path, response time. Every item from weeks one and two is a reason to trust you.

tasks.title: Add your COI as an attachment you can send in one click
Count it: leads added, touches logged, replies received
tasks.detail: It's in the Activity tab.

tasks.title: Which ICP replied most? Do more of that next week.
Build a list of 15 assisted living and senior living facilities
Build a list of 15 probate and estate attorneys
tasks.detail: Estate cleanouts and unattended deaths flow through them.

tasks.title: Add both to the dashboard
Post an educational piece, not a gore piece
tasks.detail: What families should know about who pays for cleanup. That post gets shared by the exact people who refer you.

tasks.title: Log it in the Brand Kit tab

days.focus: Get in front of someone in person

tasks.title: Walk into three funeral homes with packets
tasks.detail: Ten minutes each, no appointment, ask for the director, leave the packet. In this industry face-to-face beats fifty emails.

tasks.title: Log all three as in-person touches
Write your insurance billing process
tasks.detail: Homeowners policies often cover biohazard remediation. Knowing how to bill a claim is a selling point to every property manager.

tasks.title: Find three local independent adjusters and add them as leads
Clear the Briefing
tasks.detail: Every overdue follow-up, closed out.

tasks.title: Third touch on the funeral homes from day 15
tasks.detail: Most partnerships form on touch three to five. Almost everyone quits at one.

tasks.title: Ask anyone you've worked for to leave a Google review
tasks.detail: Even one job. Even a friend's rental turnover. A profile with zero reviews loses to a profile with three.

tasks.title: Save your best client feedback into Second Brain for use in marketing
Time yourself on a full call-to-truck-rolling drill
tasks.detail: Phone rings at 2am. What do you say, what do you grab, how fast can you be moving? Write the script.

tasks.title: Save it as Intake Call Script in Second Brain
tasks.detail: You will be half asleep when you need it.

tasks.title: Pull the numbers from the Activity tab
tasks.detail: Leads added, touches made, replies, meetings, jobs.

tasks.title: Which channel produced the replies?
tasks.detail: That's where month two goes.

tasks.title: Confirm every compliance item is closed
tasks.detail: Insurance bound, waste registration filed, exposure control plan written, fit test done. If any are still open, they're day one of next month.

tasks.title: Set your month two target
tasks.detail: One number. Signed referral partners is the right one at this stage, not revenue.

tasks.title: Tell Claude what happened and get the next thirty days built

ongoing.note: After day 30 the email switches to this weekly rhythm.

tasks.title: Set this week's outreach target and pick the ICP you're pushing
Add 10 new leads to the dashboard, all with follow-up dates
Clear every overdue follow-up, then send 10 first touches
Three drop-in visits with packets. Log all three.
Post once and log it in Brand Kit
Clear the Briefing. Check insurance, registrations and renewals.
Clear anything overdue. Otherwise rest — you're on call.
